newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Canada group mulls Brazil B Band ruling response.
newsitem.headline: Canada group mulls Brazil B Band ruling response.

text.p: A consortium including BCE Inc's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc unit TIW International said it will study a Brazilian court ruling barring it from bidding on two cellular concessions before deciding whether to appeal.

The Telet group's lawyers "know the decision was taken but they're awaiting official notification so they can analyze it before deciding what to do next," said Elio Sussekind, a spokesman for the consortium.

A Superior Justice Tribunal judge Friday ruled in the government's favor by snuffing an injunction that allowed the Telet group to continue bidding for concessions despite being disqualified by the Communications Ministry.
"The injunction was overruled and Telet cannot bid for the concessions," a court spokesman said.

Analysts said it is unclear if Telet will appeal before bidding August 11 on the concession to operate B Band services in Sao Palo state or what will happen next as the court has yet to rule on Telet's appeal of the disqualification.
Sussekind said the consortium's lawyers wanted to study the ruling before deciding what to do next.
Friday's court decision was the latest twist in an increasingly public dispute between the Telet group and Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
Motta ruled in June that Telet could not take part in bids for concessions to provide B Band cellular services in three regions which cover Sao Paulo city, Sao Paulo state and Rio de Janeiro state.

Telet then won an injunction that allowed it to continue in the bidding process, pending a future ruling on the merit of its appeal. Although a group including BellSouth Corp won the Sao Paulo city concession earlier this month, Telet had remained in the running for the other two concessions.
Officials from the Telet group complained they were unfairly disqualifed by the minister, despite having been earlier approved for participation in bidding process by a ministry committee.
In a statement, the tribunal said the judge agreed with the government's argument that Telet lacked technical experience to handle the three biggest B Band contracts.

Telet remains in the running for three smaller concessions. Another group, Americel, which comprises the same members as Telet, has already been awarded a B Band concession for a region in centerwestern Brazil which includes Brasilia.
